screening.reason: Reports a diagnostic-prediction (ASD vs NC classification) analysis of ABIDE resting-state fMRI DMN BOLD signals, satisfying inclusion 2-3.

evidence_spans.text: The sample size is 82 subjects (41 ASD and 41 normal cases) collected from three different sites  of Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE).
evidence_spans.claim: Cohort: 82 subjects (41 ASD/41 NC) from three ABIDE sites.

evidence_spans.text: The resting-state fMRI data of 41 ASD and 41 normal control (NC) cases were gathered from the Autism Brain  Image Data Exchange (ABIDE) sources [16], taken from multiple independent neuroimaging sites.
evidence_spans.claim: Final sample confirmed as 41 ASD/41 NC across independent sites.

evidence_spans.text:
The DPARSF is a MATLAB toolbox for fMRI data pre-
processing and analysing [17].
The  automated anatomical labelling (AAL) is selected as the standard brain atlas to divide the brain into 116 regions of  interest (ROIs)
evidence_spans.claim: Used the AAL atlas (116 ROIs), with 22 DMN ROIs selected for analysis.

evidence_spans.text: The extracted features are trained  using two classifiers: support vector machine (SVM) and K-nearest neighbours (KNN). The best prediction results  are 85.9% accuracy achieved by extracted the features from DenseNet201 network and classified these features by  KNN classifier.
evidence_spans.claim: Best classification result: 85.9% accuracy using DenseNet201-extracted features with a KNN classifier.

assessments.support: Site-level N given (CALTECH, CMU, KKI) but no explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria beyond sourcing from ABIDE are described.
DPARSF preprocessing steps and AAL-atlas DMN ROI selection described in detail; scalogram time-frequency feature extraction via pretrained CNNs is clearly specified.
ASD/NC diagnosis is taken from the ABIDE source without restating the diagnostic instrument.

No explicit motion/FD-based quality-control threshold is reported; the headline 85.9% accuracy figure appears to be from a single evaluation while k-fold (5/10/15-fold) cross-validation results are reported separately in a table at similar accuracy (~85-87%), but with only N=82 total subjects and no leave-site-out evaluation across the three pooled sites.

risk_of_bias.summary: A small (N=82), three-site pooled ABIDE classification study with a clearly described CNN-feature/KNN pipeline but no motion-QC threshold, no leave-site-out evaluation, and reliance on a relatively small sample for deep pretrained-CNN feature extraction.

charting.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Based on Wavelet Transform of BOLD fMRI Signals Using Pre-trained Convolution Neural Network
charting.dataset_openly_available: Uses public ABIDE data; no data/code availability statement or repository link found in the text
charting.specific_features: DMN (22 ROIs from AAL 116-ROI atlas) BOLD signal time series converted to scalogram images via wavelet transform
charting.feature_extraction_tools: DPARSF preprocessing; AAL atlas; pretrained CNNs (GoogLeNet, DenseNet201, ResNet18, ResNet101) for feature extraction from scalograms
charting.model_category: Pretrained CNN feature extraction + SVM/KNN classifier
charting.specific_algorithms: DenseNet201/ResNet18/ResNet101/GoogLeNet feature extraction; SVM and KNN classifiers
charting.validation_methodology: k-fold cross-validation (5-, 10-, 15-fold reported in a results table)
charting.key_performance_results: Best result: 85.9% accuracy (DenseNet201 features + KNN); 10-fold CV DenseNet201+KNN: 86.5 +/- 2.4% accuracy, 86.6 +/- 3.4% sensitivity, 86.6 +/- 2.3% specificity, 86.6 +/- 2.5% precision
charting.summary_key_findings: Using DMN BOLD signals from 41 ASD and 41 NC subjects (3 ABIDE sites), wavelet scalogram images classified via pretrained-CNN (DenseNet201) features and a KNN classifier achieved up to 85.9% accuracy (86.5% with 10-fold cross-validation), outperforming prior functional-connectivity-based ABIDE classifiers cited by the authors (66.9-70.2%).
charting.future_directions_recommended: A larger sample across more ABIDE sites recommended by the authors for a more robust model

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE, 3 sites (CALTECH, CMU, KKI); n=41 ASD / 41 NC (N=82).
narrative_row.methods: DPARSF preprocessing; AAL atlas (22 DMN ROIs); BOLD time series converted to wavelet scalogram images; pretrained CNN (DenseNet201/ResNet/GoogLeNet) feature extraction; SVM/KNN classification with k-fold cross-validation.
narrative_row.outcomes: Best accuracy 85.9% (DenseNet201 + KNN), 86.5% with 10-fold cross-validation, exceeding cited prior ABIDE functional-connectivity classifiers (66.9-70.2%).
narrative_row.key_limitations: Small sample (N=82) from only 3 sites; no motion/QC threshold reported; no leave-site-out evaluation; no code/data release.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: A DMN time-frequency/CNN-transfer-learning approach to ABIDE ASD classification, with a small, modest, non-reconstructible cohort.

kg_link.cohort_description: Three ABIDE sites (CALTECH, CMU, KKI); 41 ASD and 41 NC subjects; no explicit exclusion rule beyond site/subject counts.
kg_link.finding: DMN BOLD scalogram images classified via pretrained DenseNet201 features and a KNN classifier achieved 85.9% accuracy (86.5% with 10-fold cross-validation) for ASD vs NC classification.
